protocol.name: pac_window_workspaces_v1
protocol.copyright: The pac tools. Private to them: pacland implements it, pacbar uses it.

description.summary: the workspaces and the process of a window, and moving it

protocol.description: Adds to a zwlr_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 what that protocol lacks: the workspaces the window belongs to, the process it belongs to, and a request to move it to another. The window's title, app id and output stay in the foreign toplevel protocol. A panel showing the windows of each workspace uses this to place them and to let the user drag one to another workspace.

entry.name: too_many
entry.summary: too many objects for one window

request.name: get_window
request.description: A client may have a few objects for the same window. If the toplevel is already closed the object is created and stays silent.

event.name: workspaces

description.summary: the workspaces the window belongs to

event.description: Bit n-1 is workspace n of the window's output. Sent when the object is created and each time the set changes; at least one bit is set.

request.name: move

description.summary: move the window to a workspace

request.description: The window now belongs to that workspace only (1 to 10), as the keyboard action "move window to N", and the compositor keeps the focus consistent. Ignored when the window is gone or the session is locked.

event.name: pid

description.summary: the process that owns the window

event.description: The process id of the client that made the window (an X11 window: the process its client says it is). Sent when the object is created, once, and only when it is known; a window of a client that is gone, or one that the compositor cannot tell, has none. Windows of one program share it, so it says which program, not which window; the program's helper processes have other ids.
